steps.title: Check the Wi-Fi switch and airplane mode
steps.detail: Make sure the laptop's Wi-Fi switch or function key is turned on and airplane mode is off. Look for the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar to confirm it is active.

steps.title: Forget and rejoin the Wi-Fi network
steps.detail: Open Wi-Fi settings, select the network, choose Forget, then reconnect and enter the Wi-Fi password again. This resets the saved connection settings that may have become unstable.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update or your system's update settings and install any available updates. Network driver updates often fix dropped connections.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop completely. This clears temporary network problems and reconnects to the Wi-Fi network after startup.

steps.title: Check which Wi-Fi network you are connected to
steps.detail: Click the Wi-Fi icon and look at the network name shown as connected. If it says Guest or is not your usual office or home network, it is the wrong one.

steps.title: Forget the guest network and rejoin your main network
steps.detail: Open Wi-Fi settings, select the guest network and choose Forget. Then pick your usual network from the list, enter its password, and check that the internet works.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: If the internet still does not work after rejoining your usual network, restart the computer. Then check the Wi-Fi name and try a website again.

steps.detail: Click the airplane icon at the bottom right, or open the Action Center, and make sure airplane mode is switched off. Wi-Fi cannot find networks while airplane mode is on.

steps.title: Check the Wi-Fi switch
steps.detail: Look for a physical Wi-Fi switch on the side of the laptop, or a key with a Wi-Fi symbol that works together with the Fn key. Make sure it is turned on.

steps.title: Turn Wi-Fi off and back on
steps.detail: Open the Wi-Fi quick settings from the bottom right corner, switch Wi-Fi off, wait a few seconds, and then switch it back on. Wait a moment for the list of networks to appear.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop from the Start menu. After it starts up again, check whether your Wi-Fi networks are listed.

steps.title: Check the paper tray and load paper
steps.detail: The orange blinking light usually means the printer is out of paper. Refill the tray with paper, make sure it sits flat and is pushed fully in, then try printing again.

steps.title: Make sure all covers and doors are closed
steps.detail: Look for any open cover or door on the printer, and close it firmly. Printers often blink orange when a cover is open or paper is stuck inside.

steps.title: Cancel stuck print jobs
steps.detail: Open the printer queue from your computer's printer list and cancel any jobs waiting there. Then send one test page to see whether the printer responds.

steps.title: Turn the printer off and back on
steps.detail: Switch the printer off with its power button, wait about 30 seconds, then switch it back on. Give it a few minutes to warm up before trying to print again.

steps.title: Check the printer for errors, paper and toner
steps.detail: Look at the printer's display or lights for an error message. Make sure there is paper in the tray and that the toner or ink is not empty.

steps.title: Cancel the stuck job in the print queue
steps.detail: Open the printer queue from your computer's printer settings, select the stuck document and choose Cancel. This removes only the print job, so the other jobs behind it can then go through.

steps.title: Turn the printer off and back on
steps.detail: Switch the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, then switch it on again. Wait for it to finish starting up before you send the document again.

steps.title: Restart the computer and print again
steps.detail: Restart your computer to clear any stuck printing software. After it starts up, send the document to the printer again.

steps.title: Check the ink or toner level
steps.detail: Look at the printer's display or the printer software on your computer to see how much ink or toner is left. If a level is low, replace the cartridge or order a new one.

steps.title: Set the print quality to high
steps.detail: Open the print settings from the print window and choose a higher quality option, such as Best or High, instead of Draft. Then print the page again.

steps.title: Check the paper type setting
steps.detail: Make sure the paper type selected in the print settings matches the paper in the tray. A mismatch can cause light or streaky output.

steps.title: Run the printer's cleaning cycle
steps.detail: Open the printer's maintenance or tools menu, either on the printer itself or in its software, and start the cleaning or head cleaning option. Print a test page when it finishes.

steps.title: Unplug and plug the USB headset back in
steps.detail: Remove the headset from the USB port, wait a few seconds, then push it firmly into a port. Check that the plug is fully seated.

steps.title: Try a different USB port
steps.detail: Move the headset to another USB port on the laptop. Some ports may not respond well to audio devices.

steps.title: Set the headset as the default playback device
steps.detail: Open the sound settings from the taskbar speaker icon and choose the headset under output devices. This tells the laptop to send sound to the headset instead of the speakers.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Restart the computer with the headset still plugged in. This lets the laptop detect the device fresh when it starts up.

steps.title: Check the sound output device
steps.detail: Open the sound settings from the speaker icon in the taskbar and confirm the correct output device, such as Speakers or Headphones, is selected. Play a short sound to check that it can be heard.

steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the whole laptop. After it starts up, play a video or test sound to see if it works.

steps.title: Check for a privacy shutter or camera switch
steps.detail: Look at the top edge of the laptop screen for a small sliding cover or a camera on/off key. Make sure the cover is open and the camera is turned on.

steps.title: Close other apps that might be using the camera
steps.detail: Close any other video, photo or recording apps, and any browser tabs that may be using the camera. Then open your video call again.

steps.title: Restart the video call app
steps.detail: Close the video call app completely, then open it again and start the call. Check whether the camera picture appears.

steps.title: Check camera permission for the app
steps.detail: Open the Windows Settings camera page and make sure camera access is turned on for your video call app. Then restart the app.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update and install any available updates, then try the video call again. Updates can fix camera driver problems.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop. Try the video call again after it starts up.

steps.title: Check the microphone mute settings
steps.detail: Make sure the mute button on your headset or keyboard is off, and that the microphone icon in the Teams meeting toolbar is not crossed out. Unmute yourself if needed.

steps.title: Quit and reopen Teams
steps.detail: Close Teams completely, including from the system tray near the clock, then open it again. Join a test call to check whether people can hear you.

steps.title: Select the correct microphone in Teams
steps.detail: In Teams, open Settings, then Devices, and choose the microphone you are actually speaking into from the Microphone list. Use the test call option to confirm the level bar moves when you talk.

steps.title: Unplug and plug back in your headset or microphone
steps.detail: Disconnect the USB headset or microphone, wait a few seconds, and plug it back into the same port. If it is connected to a dock or hub, try plugging it directly into the computer instead.

steps.title: Check the input volume in Windows
steps.detail: Open Sound settings from the taskbar speaker icon and look under Input. Confirm the correct microphone is selected and that its volume bar moves when you speak.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the computer. After it starts up, test your microphone in a Teams test call before joining a meeting.

steps.title: Check that both ends of the video cable are firmly plugged in
steps.detail: Unplug the cable from the laptop and the monitor, then push each end in until it clicks or sits snugly. Make sure it is in the port on the laptop and the matching port on the monitor.

steps.title: Select the correct input on the monitor
steps.detail: Press the Input or Source button on the monitor and choose the port your cable uses, such as HDMI or DisplayPort. The monitor shows 'No signal' when it is set to a different input.

steps.title: Detect the second display from the laptop
steps.detail: Press Windows key + P and choose Extend or Duplicate. If the monitor still doesn't appear, open Settings > System > Display and select Detect or Find.

steps.title: Restart the laptop with the monitor connected
steps.detail: Keep the monitor plugged in and restart the laptop. Once it starts again, check whether the monitor shows an image.

steps.title: Check the mouse receiver is plugged in firmly
steps.detail: Unplug the small USB receiver from the computer and plug it back into a different USB port. Press it all the way in so it sits snugly.

steps.title: Check the mouse has power
steps.detail: Make sure the mouse's power switch is turned on. If it has batteries, check they are inserted correctly and replace them if they seem weak.

steps.title: Unplug and replug the USB receiver
steps.detail: Unplug the receiver, wait about ten seconds, then plug it back in. Windows should recognize it again within a few seconds.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Restart the computer with the receiver still plugged in. This often reconnects the mouse after a stuck driver or sleep problem.

steps.title: Check the Num Lock and keyboard language
steps.detail: Make sure Caps Lock is off and the keyboard language is set correctly in the taskbar. A wrong language setting can make typed letters look wrong.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the computer so it detects the keyboard again. Test the keyboard after it starts up.

steps.title: Press the brightness-up key
steps.detail: Press the brightness-up key on your keyboard, usually marked with a sun icon, possibly while holding the Fn key. Press it several times to see if the screen gets brighter.

steps.title: Turn off battery saver and adaptive brightness
steps.detail: Open Settings, go to Display, and check the brightness slider. Turn off any Adaptive brightness or Battery saver option that may be dimming the screen, then adjust the slider.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop from the Start menu. A restart can clear a display glitch that makes the screen look dim.

steps.title: Try the company portal in another browser
steps.detail: Open Microsoft Edge or another browser you have installed and go to the portal address. If it loads properly there, you can keep working while the Chrome issue is looked at.

steps.title: Close Chrome completely and open it again
steps.detail: Close every Chrome window, then reopen Chrome and load the portal again. This clears up many one-off page loading problems.

steps.title: Clear the cached images and files in Chrome
steps.detail: In Chrome, open Settings, go to Privacy and security, choose Clear browsing data, and tick only Cached images and files. Then reload the portal.

steps.title: Check for a Chrome update
steps.detail: Select the three-dot menu, go to Help, then About Google Chrome. Let it check for updates and install any update it finds, then restart Chrome.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, restart the computer, and open the portal in Chrome again once it has started up.

steps.title: Wait a minute for Outlook to recover
steps.detail: Outlook sometimes needs a short time to finish a large task. Give it about a minute before you do anything else.

steps.title: Close and reopen Outlook
steps.detail: If it is still frozen, close Outlook from the taskbar or with Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager and end the Outlook task. Then open Outlook again.

steps.title: Check for Office and Windows updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update from the Start menu and install any available updates. Restart Outlook after the updates finish.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: If Outlook still freezes, save your open work and restart the computer. This clears problems that build up while the computer is running.

steps.title: Close Excel with Task Manager
steps.detail: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager, select Microsoft Excel in the list, and click End task. Any unsaved changes may be lost, so do this only if Excel stays frozen.

steps.title: Reopen Excel and check the file
steps.detail: Open Excel again and go to File > Open > Recent to reopen your spreadsheet. If Excel offers to recover unsaved changes, choose to open the recovered version and check that your work is there.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: If Excel freezes again, save your other work, restart the computer, and then open the spreadsheet. A restart clears memory and stuck background processes.

steps.title: Restart the computer to finish the update
steps.detail: Select Restart now from the Windows Update page or the prompt. Wait for the laptop to restart fully, then sign back in and check that the message is gone.

steps.title: Check the wall outlet and power strip
steps.detail: Make sure the outlet or power strip has its switch turned on. Plug a different device, such as a lamp or phone charger, into the same outlet to confirm it has power.

steps.title: Check the charger connections
steps.detail: Push the charger plug firmly into the laptop and the power adapter firmly into the wall or power strip. Look over the cable for bends, cuts or exposed wires, and stop using it if you see any damage.

steps.title: Try a different outlet
steps.detail: Plug the charger directly into a different wall outlet, not a power strip or extension cord. If the light comes on, the first outlet or power strip was the problem.

steps.title: Restart the laptop with the charger connected
steps.detail: Shut the laptop down completely, leave the charger plugged in, wait about 30 seconds, then turn it on again. Check whether the charging light comes on after it starts up.

steps.title: Press a key or move the mouse or touchpad
steps.detail: Press the Shift key or move the mouse or touchpad to wake the screen. Laptops often sleep after a short idle time, and this may be all it needs.

steps.title: Check any external monitor or display cable
steps.detail: If the laptop is connected to a monitor or projector, make sure the cable is firmly plugged in at both ends. Then press the Windows key and P together and choose a display option to switch the picture back to the laptop screen.

steps.title: Raise the screen brightness
steps.detail: Press the brightness-up key, usually a sun icon on the keyboard, possibly with the Fn key held down. The screen may be on but turned all the way down.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save any open work if you can, then restart the laptop. If the screen stays black, press the power button once to see whether the laptop responds, and contact a technician if it still does not show anything.

steps.title: Lower your speaker volume
steps.detail: Turn down the speaker volume on your computer or the Zoom speaker slider. Loud sound from the speakers is what the microphone picks up and sends back as an echo.

steps.title: Plug in headphones or earbuds
steps.detail: Wear headphones or earbuds, or use a headset with a built-in microphone. This keeps the sound from your speakers out of your microphone and usually stops the echo right away.

steps.title: Check the microphone and speaker in Zoom
steps.detail: In Zoom, click the arrow next to the microphone icon and choose Audio Settings. Make sure the microphone and speaker you are using are selected, and test them with the buttons shown.

steps.title: Check echo cancellation in Zoom
steps.detail: In Zoom, open Settings, go to Audio, then Advanced, and check that the echo cancellation option is set to Auto. Turn on background noise suppression if it is off.

steps.title: Restart Zoom and rejoin the call
steps.detail: Close the Zoom app completely, open it again, and join the meeting. This applies the audio settings you changed.

steps.detail: Open the VPN app's update check, or check for normal updates in your computer's update settings, and install any that are available. Then try connecting again.

steps.detail: Restart your computer, wait until it has fully started and reconnected to your home Wi-Fi, then open the VPN app and connect.

rawSteps.detail: Right-click the saved PDF, choose Open with, and pick another PDF viewer or your web browser. If it opens there, the problem is with the first program.

rawSteps.title: Check for updates to your PDF program
rawSteps.detail: Open the PDF program's Help or About menu and look for an update option, then install any normal update offered. Also check Windows Update or your software update tool for pending updates.

rawSteps.title: Restart your computer
rawSteps.detail: Save your open work, then restart the computer. Try the PDF again after it has started back up.

steps.title: Save a copy and work in the copy
steps.detail: Use File > Save As to save a new copy to your Desktop with a different name, then open and edit that copy. Your original file stays unchanged.

steps.title: Turn off the file's Read-only setting

steps.title: Check the Wi-Fi switch and airplane mode
steps.detail: Make sure the Wi-Fi switch on your laptop is on and airplane mode is off. Look at the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar to confirm you are connected.

steps.title: Forget and rejoin the office Wi-Fi network
steps.detail: Open the Wi-Fi settings, choose the office network, and select Forget. Then reconnect and enter the Wi-Fi password again.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update (or Software Update on a Mac) and install any normal updates waiting for you. Restart if asked.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the computer. Reconnect to the office Wi-Fi once it starts up and watch whether the drops continue around 1:00 pm.
